change: the AP Cyber Unit 1 in-lesson navigator stops sending students to the wrong lesson: 20 crossed lesson tabs, 71 wrong step links and 26 steps greyed out as unbuilt, across 10 live pages
_context: THE DEFECT, measured against the live storefront on 2026-09-08. 28 Unit 1
pages carry the navigator rail. 18 are correct. 10 are wrong, in three
ways that were reported as one.
1. THE 1.3 / 1.4 CROSS, on all 10 pages. The rail reads:
1.3  title="Best Practices for Public Networks"  ->  ai-driven-threats
1.4  title="AI-Based Cybersecurity Attacks"      ->  wireless-security
The CED titles are right and the hrefs are crossed, so a teacher
assigning 1.3 by its official name sends the class to the AI attacks
lesson and the tooltip agrees with them the whole way.
2. 26 STEPS GREYED OUT AS UNBUILT, on 2 of those 10:
ap-cyber-unit-1-exam          14   1.2 Lab and Quiz, then all of 1.3-1.5
ap-cyber-unit-1-lesson-2-lab  12   all of 1.3, 1.4 and 1.5
All 26 target pages answer 200 with 32KB to 75KB of real content. They
were built; the rail was frozen before they were. A student sitting on
the Unit 1 exam cannot reach three fifths of the unit.
3. THE ONE NOBODY REPORTED, and the worst of the three. 9 nav hrefs use a
retired handle convention, and following them today lands here:
1.4 Ex 1 / Ex 2 / Lab / Quiz  ->  1.3's exercise, lab and quiz  (8 pages)
1.2 Quiz                      ->  the 1.2 LESSON page          (7 pages)
So on 8 pages every one of 1.4's four activities runs 1.3's, and the
work a student does there is recorded against 1.3's item ids. 1.4 stays
empty in the gradebook while the student is sure they did it.
Classified by following each old href to its canonical destination:
79 of the 91 href changes are real misroutes, 12 are a retired handle
that already redirects to the right page and is only being shortened.
WHERE THE RIGHT ANSWER COMES FROM. Nothing here retypes a handle; retyping
is how the site ended up teaching 3.3 under 3.4's title. The target table
is built from two sources authored independently of each other:
config/cyber-topics.json for the five CED topics, and a majority vote of
every self-consistent live rail for all 25 activity rows. They agree on
every row, and the build refuses if they ever do not.
THE FIRST VERSION OF THAT CHECK WAS HOLLOW, and a mutation caught it. It
picked its witnesses by agreement with the CED and then checked the
survivors against the CED, so breaking the taxonomy on purpose excluded
every page and reported 'no live page supplies a target' instead of a
disagreement. The taxonomy could not be contradicted by the thing meant to
contradict it. The live pages now vote without the CED touching who is
eligible, which is why the 10 swapped pages get a vote and lose it 18 to 10.
AND THE SHEET WAS BUILT FROM THE WRONG SOURCE TWICE OVER. Generating it
from the rendered page produced a different file on every run:
data-cfemail="3f535550515a4c7f4c5c57505053115a5b4a"   first run
data-cfemail="325e585d5c57417241515a5d5d5e1c575647"   second run
Cloudflare obfuscates addresses at render time and rerolls the XOR key per
response, so the rendered body is neither stable nor the body Shopify
stores. Importing it would have made that rewrite permanent. The generator
reads /pages/<handle>.json instead, which storefront-fetch already names
the preferred source for anything that writes a body back. Two live runs
now produce the same md5, and the sheet carries zero Cloudflare artefacts.
THE REWRITE IS NARROW ON PURPOSE. The 10 bad pages carry an older rail
generation and it would be tempting to replace the whole thing. Three
kinds of byte change and no others: a lesson anchor href, a step anchor
href, and a disabled span becoming an anchor. Every byte outside the rail
comes out identical, and verify() proves that by re-parsing the output
rather than trusting the rewriter.

checks.name: the census, the repair, the invariants and nine mutations one rule at a time
checks._why: A floor rather than the exact 26, per scripts/gate-suite-floor.js. The post-deploy run of the lab lock gate refused a correct deploy over smoke:storefront reading 93 where its manifest pinned 90, because main had gained a verifier while the pull request was open. This gate is not satisfied until its live check runs after the Matrixify import, so it has exactly that window open. Matching ", 0 failed" instead would be worse: a suite that stopped running its assertions reports zero failures too, and this repo has found three hollow guards that way.

checks.name: the sheet clears the Matrixify preflight
checks._why: --carrying supplies the captured before-bodies so the preflight can prove the one emoji and the 698 non-ASCII characters were already on the page rather than introduced. With no original the safe reading of a raw emoji is that a generator added it, and the preflight refuses.
checks.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const d='smoke/fixtures/live-bodies/cyber-u1-nav';const o={};for(const f of fs.readdirSync(d))if(f.endsWith('.html'))o[f.replace(/\\.html$/,'')]=fs.readFileSync(d+'/'+f,'utf8');fs.mkdirSync('.work',{recursive:true});fs.writeFileSync('.work/u1-nav-carrying.json',JSON.stringify(o));" && node scripts/matrixify-preflight.js imports/2026-09-08/cyber-u1-nav-repair-pages.csv --expect-command MERGE --carrying .work/u1-nav-carrying.json

checks.name: a second implementation in Python reaches the same counts from the raw CSV
checks._why: Its own CSV reader, its own container-based rail parser (the JS slices between lesson anchors; this walks the ucn-steps containers, the other half of the same structure), its own style-attribute parser instead of a regex, and its lesson titles read from the CED extract text rather than the taxonomy JSON. It re-derives 26 disabled, 2 pages, 20 crossed tabs and 71 wrong hrefs before, and zero of each after, with no import of the rewriter.

checks.name: the live verifier goes green on the repaired bodies, using the same assertions that will judge the deploy
checks._why: The pre-check and the post-check are the SAME program, pointed at a directory instead of the storefront. Without that they would be two different programs and the claim that the sheet turns the deploy green would rest on nothing. Against the live pages this same command reports 1 passed, 5 failed.
checks.command: node -e "const nav=require('./lib/cyber-u1-nav.js'),g=require('./scripts/cyber-u1-nav-repair-csv.js'),fs=require('fs');const b={};for(const f of fs.readdirSync(g.FIXDIR))if(f.endsWith('.html'))b[f.replace(/\\.html$/,'')]=fs.readFileSync(g.FIXDIR+'/'+f,'utf8');const{table}=g.buildTable(b);fs.mkdirSync('.work/u1-repaired',{recursive:true});for(const[h,x]of Object.entries(b))fs.writeFileSync('.work/u1-repaired/'+h+'.html',nav.audit(nav.parse(x),table).length?nav.repair(x,table).out:x);" && node scripts/verify-cyber-u1-nav-live.js --from .work/u1-repaired

checks.name: THE ONE MY OWN FIRST CENSUS GOT WRONG: a whitespace-blind disabled detector
checks._why: The two live pages spell the same inline style differently, opacity:0.4 on the exam and opacity: 0.4 on lesson-2-lab. A detector written against one of them reports the other page clean, which is exactly what my first census did: it found 14 disabled steps and the true answer is 26. This is the mutation that matters most, because the guard looked complete and was not.

checks.name: prefix-match the step class again and the containers count as steps
checks._why: class="ucn-step" and class="ucn-steps" differ by one letter, and the container holds the five steps. Matching the class as a prefix makes a container parse as a step and the census collapses.

checks.name: stop refusing a near-tie and the table guesses a handle out of a coin flip
checks.expect_failure: a near-tie among the live pages is refused rather than guessed

checks.name: stop comparing the CED taxonomy against the live majority
checks._why: This is the check whose first version was hollow. With it gone, a taxonomy naming the wrong page for a topic would be laundered into 10 live bodies without a word.
checks.expect_failure: a live page disagreeing with the CED taxonomy is refused

checks.name: stop checking that nothing outside the rail moved
checks._why: The whole safety case for touching 10 live bodies is that only the rail changes. Without this the rewriter could edit a lesson and every href check would still pass.
checks.find: if (before.slice(rb.end) !== after.slice(ra.end)) fails.push('bytes after the rail changed');
checks.replace: if (false) fails.push('bytes after the rail changed');
checks.expect_failure: a byte changed outside the rail is caught

checks.name: the live navigator no longer crosses 1.3 and 1.4, greys out a built page, or sends 1.4 to 1.3
checks._why: Every assertion is FALSE on the pages as they serve today (1 passed, 5 failed) and TRUE once the sheet is imported in MERGE mode. Run it before the import as the pre-check and again afterwards.

not_covered: Whether the rail's tooltips are the right words. The 10 repaired pages carry the CED titles and the 18 correct pages carry site nicknames (1.3 reads 'Public Wi-Fi Dangers' there, not 'Best Practices for Public Networks'). Both point at the right page after this change, so navigation is correct either way, and picking one wording for the whole unit is a content decision rather than a link fix.

The older rail generation itself. The 10 repaired pages still use span containers, a non-link current step and no onclick on the lesson anchor, where the 18 correct pages use div containers and a linked current step. Rewriting them to the newer generation would change markup nobody has measured on pages that are otherwise fine, so this changes hrefs and nothing else.
Units 2 through 5. Only Unit 1 rails were read. The same defect could sit in any of them and this says nothing about it.

ap-cyber-unit-1-lesson-2-terminal-lab, which the practice hub links and the rail does not. It answers 200 with a 4.5KB body where every other activity page is 32KB to 75KB, so it looks like a shell, but that is a separate question from where the rail points.

The Unit 1 exam answer key. It was checked because it had been reported as 60 percent B and it is not: the live key is BDBADABBDCBDCCADBCCA, A:4 B:6 C:5 D:5, longest run 2, worst self-similarity 37 percent against a 55 percent limit, and the repo's own audit() returns no problems. Re-derived a second way from the distractor rationales, which name every wrong option: 16 of 20 resolve to exactly one letter and it matches the key every time, and on all 20 the keyed answer is never explained as a distractor, so nothing is mis-keyed. The 4 that do not resolve are questions with fewer than three distractor rationales, which is a content gap and not a key defect.

Whether Units 2 to 5 should be gated. They are not: ap-cyber-unit-2-exam, ap-cyber-unit-2-lesson-1-quiz, ap-cyber-unit-2-lesson-1-exercise-1 and ap-cybersecurity-unit-2-practice all answer 200 to an anonymous request, exactly as Unit 1 does. That is a pricing decision, not a link fix.
